moved.sentence: Thin but complete: one real path through every layer and boundary (UI → API → store → deploy), not a finished feature — connect the architecture before investing in any single part.

judged.note: The rule keeps at SHOULD the thin-but-complete thread: one real path through every layer and boundary, not a finished feature, connecting the architecture before investing in any part.

moved.sentence: This is the balance with YAGNI: build the shell only for the path you are committed to and that is expensive to wire up later.

judged.note: The rule keeps the YAGNI balance and building the shell only for the committed path that is expensive to wire up later, at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Do not pre-build features, options, or abstractions you don't yet need — that remains YAGNI.

judged.note: The rule keeps not pre-building unneeded features, options or abstractions as SHOULD NOT, with the that-remains-YAGNI framing.

moved.sentence: Front-load the risky integrations: the thread should pierce the boundaries most likely to surprise you (auth, third-party APIs, the deploy pipeline), so failures surface while they are cheap.

judged.note: The rule keeps at SHOULD piercing the boundaries most likely to surprise (auth, third-party APIs, deploy pipeline), with the cheap-failure reason.

moved.sentence: For agents: validate the end-to-end shape before spending effort on breadth, so a wrong architecture is caught early instead of after generating volume against it.

judged.note: The rule keeps the for-agents scope and validating the end-to-end shape before breadth at SHOULD, with the catch-a-wrong-architecture-early reason.
